image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Large rectangular steel refuse container with two hinged flat lids meeting at the centre, sloped front face, welded corner posts and side lifting trunnions, four small castor wheels underneath Materials: chipped blue municipal paint over heavy rust, bare metal along the lid edges, grime and drip streaks down the front.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- the five layers mean 0.922 and the three critical features 0.933. 1,068/2,000 triangles, 3/3 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/4 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. The only budget axis this round moved was maxMaterials, 2 -> 3, and it is what let the lids be re-based to their own probed envelope. What is still simplified: the plate's corner hinge STRAPS are a bracket plate and a trunnion block rather than a strap, and its drips are more concentrated below the handle bar than the tile's.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 1.40 x 1.393 x 0.6475 m at the corrected declaration. The BODY TAPER was rebuilt: the first build shipped B0W/BW 0.954 (near-vertical sides) on the Meshy proxy's band table, which reads w 0.874-0.934 from band 1 to 8. The PLATE contradicts it, and the proxy is wrong -- a row scan (scratch/_taper.mjs) reads the front face narrowing 899 px at the rim (frac 0.30) to 628 px at the body base (frac 0.85), 0.699 raw. The plate's own top deck fixes the perspective share: its back edge is 0.814 of its front edge over 0.65 m of depth, giving a camera 2.85 m out, so the base -- 1.10 m lower -- loses a further 0.838 at 30 deg elevation. Real taper 0.699/0.838 = 0.833 (0.79 at 20 deg, 0.85 at 35), now shipped as B0W 1.08 / B0D 0.50.
featureReviews.notes: The band table against the proxy is now WORSE by construction (the proxy has no taper) and that is the correct outcome: matching it at 0.0186 mean delta was two wrong numbers agreeing. Elevation is bounded, not solved, so the taper carries a 0.79-0.85 range.

featureReviews.evidence: Two lids as a two-instance InstancedMesh at x +-0.255: one flat 0.50 x 0.03 x 0.47 plate with its two outer corners chamfered 70 mm (v3), the right instance yawed PI, over fixed hinge barrels on the fittings; lid-hinge-l/-r at (+-0.255, 1.375, -0.26) axis X. Extents measured off a crop of the plate's top deck (scratch/_lidcrop.png) at the LIDS' OWN row, where the deck spans crop x 110-1000 and the lids 205-885: 0.764, against the 0.924 the first build shipped.
featureReviews.notes: The lids are on their OWN material now and their tone was PROBED rather than corrected. They had no `uv` directive at all, so the chipping on their material never reached them -- over the lid's own crop the plate is 16.7% warm pixels and the build returned 0.3%. And their top face is where the harness's additive term is largest: two authored values 32 counts apart came back 8 apart, fitting R = 0.5625A + 118, G = 0.50A + 116, B = 0.375A + 132, so the shipped #a3cce3 rendered them 216/219/221 -- neutral WHITE, 28 luma over the plate's 166/198/217, with the blue gone -- and no small correction reaches the measurement when a third of every channel arrives from the light. No swing flap: the plate has none, so no flap pivot.

featureReviews.evidence: Round orange bar r 0.022 x 1.02 m at 0.70 m on flat lugs and a round lift grip r 0.020 x 0.16 m at 0.93 m on two stubs (v3; #b8703f from region-orange 0.829). The rust is now the plate's MEASURED #8a4a22 exactly, which the first build could not reach: a canvas tile is a MULTIPLY, and ratio(#8a4a22, #2f6a95) is (2.94, 0.70, 0.23) -- red above 1, so it clamped and left green dominant, which is what shipped as grey-green smudges. The body is now its own component on its own material re-based to the per-channel ENVELOPE #8a6a95, with the blue field painted BY the tile (base fill 0.341, 1, 1); that renders the body back to #2f6a95 and the rust to #8a4a22 exactly. The pale lids need no re-basing -- ratio(#8a4a22, #a3cce3) is (0.847, 0.363, 0.150), every channel under 1 -- so their chipping is a plain multiply on the shared material.
featureReviews.notes: The LIDS are now re-based too, and for the same reason the body was: inverting their probed transfer, the plate's lid blue (151,198,227) wants (59,164,253) authored and its lid rust (225,173,143) wants (190,114,29), which are not orderings of each other. Envelope #bea4fd, base fill (0.308, 1, 1), rust (1, 0.695, 0.115). Shipped they measure 155/191/214 blue and 12.6% warm pixels against the plate's 151/198/227 and 16.8%. This is what maxMaterials 2 -> 3 buys and it costs no draw call: the lids are already their own InstancedMesh, and they cannot share `steel` (a re-based base fill of 0.308 in red would take the orange handle bar and the castors down with it) or `bodypaint` (a different envelope and a different fill). The cluster OPACITY is a new defaulted parameter on paintTile: the tile composites source-over, so at the 0.30 default a cluster blends to an intermediate tone and only its specks reach the authored rust -- right for a bloom on painted steel, wrong for a lid whose paint has come off. The BODY does not get that lift and the ceiling is the turntable gate: at 0.55 the cluster cores render 74/61/55 on the shaded front, 22 counts of city-block distance from the harness backdrop's own (58,58,58), and the gate segmented 3,890 px of the front face as interior HOLES at azimuth 0 in a pattern that overlays the clusters exactly. Castors and corner fittings are held on CHROMA, not lifted: the turntable gate's background test is |luma-58| <= 24 AND sat <= 0.16, so #3f4a5c (luma 76, sat 0.315) and #4a5568 (luma 87, sat 0.29) keep the plate's DARK hardware and still clear it. A neutral #6a6f76 was read as a 2,100 px hole at azimuth 90 and 270.

name: Municipal Steel Dumpster
nameTh: ถังขยะเหล็กขนาดใหญ่
notes: The steel bins the municipal trucks lift at markets and behind shophouse rows. Two lids hinge along the back top edge: ships a root pivot plus lid-hinge-l and lid-hinge-r pivots on the rear top rail and no sockets. Not breakable. Box collider is the full body. Declared size corrected 1.80 x 1.30 x 1.10 -> 1.40 x 1.40 x 0.65 at model time (2026-08-27): the Meshy proxy band table reads w/h 0.91 and d/h 0.46 in every band, and the plate itself (high camera, vertical foreshortened ~0.8) shows a container as tall as it is wide with a top face ~0.45 of its width deep; 1.80 x 1.30 would be a squat box the plate does not show. The medium budget class is kept. maxDrawCalls raised 2 -> 3 (2026-09-01) so the BODY can be its own component on its own material: a canvas tile is a MULTIPLY and can only darken, so orange rust (#8a4a22, red 138) cannot be painted onto the shipped blue (#2f6a95, red 47) at all -- ratio red is 2.94, it clamps, and the marks render olive, which is exactly what the first build shipped as grey-green smudges. The body's own material is re-based to the envelope #8a6a95 with the blue field painted BY the tile (base fill 0.341,1,1), which renders the body back to #2f6a95 and the rust to the plate's measured #8a4a22 exactly. The third draw call buys the prop's identity-defining weathering; the other two components (fittings, and the two lids as one InstancedMesh) are unchanged.
